text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up. Proposal: split Dedicated autoscaler into two composable controllers: a planner that emits high-level intents, and an executor that converts intents into operator actions. Keeps heuristics separate from ops plumbing. Thoughts?

aj: Sounds good. Easier to iterate heuristics in planner without touching operator.

simon: Agree in principle. Important design Q: how expressive is the intent? A small surface (capacity + SLO) or detailed placement (pods, shards, GPUs)?

maria: My preference: keep intent abstract and implementation-agnostic. Example fields: "target_capacity": 240, "min_ready": 10, "slo_hint": "p99-latency". Executor maps that to placement/packing.

kevin: Keep planner minimal. Only emit desired capacity, SLO hint, and optional deadline. Executor should own packing, thermal constraints, and quota checks. That keeps the planner model cheap.

ashley: Planner should also suggest preferred_prewarms and credit_hint so executor can check tenant prewarm tokens. But executor decides whether to honor based on safety.

simon: We need explicit fallback semantics in the intent. If executor cannot satisfy it (quota, regional limits), what should it do? Options: degrade_capacity, route_to_queue, or fail-open.
maria: Add a "fallback_policy" field with enumerated choices. Planner picks preference; executor enforces safety and reports back.

aj: How do we surface intent vs applied state in observability? We need time-series of intended_capacity vs applied_capacity for alerts and billing reconciliation.
maria: Executor should report status: "applied_capacity", "applied_prewarms", "rejection_reason" (if any). Both planner_intent and executor_status stored in control plane for audit.

kevin: Rollout idea: planner-only mode first (planner writes intents to store, executor is a noop). Validate intents and metrics in staging. Next, enable executor in canary (one shard) and monitor applied vs intended.
simon: Also add chaos tests: slow node provisioning, partial prewarm failure, quota denial. Verify planner backoff and recovery.

ashley: Implementation notes: planner cadence ~30s, idempotent outputs (include intent_id). Executor APIs must accept idempotency_key and be replay-safe.
maria: We should define a compact, versioned proto/json schema for intent/status (v1) so we can extend fields later.

aj: Security: who can mutate intents? Only planner should normally write. Allow ops to create annotated override intents (write-once annotation) with RBAC checks. Documented audit trail needed.

kevin: Metrics to surface: planner_predicted_cost_delta, planner_risk_score, planner_time_to_ready_est. Executor exposes start_time, applied_cost, applied_nodes.

ashley: API surface proposal for the operator: POST /intents/apply {intent, idempotency_key} -> 202 + op_id; GET /intents/status/{op_id} for reconciliation. That keeps executor decoupled and observable.
simon: Prewarm accounting: executor must atomically debit tenant prewarm credits when committing prewarms. Avoid races/double-consumption.

maria: Action items: 1) ashley: draft intent/status proto v1 (due EOD Thu). 2) simon: failure-mode test matrix (due Mon). 3) kevin: canary rollout plan + dashboard (due next Wed). 4) aj: RBAC/override doc (due Fri).

deploy-bot: planner-service v0.1 deployed to staging at 1746601258 :rocket:
aj: I'll open a tiny PR to wire planner -> intent-store in staging so we can watch emitted intents in console.
maria: Thanks. Please keep design questions here; we'll iterate on the proto and fallback enum. :raised_hands:
